full_judgment: 16. We observe that in facilitating the agenda and process of privatisation to the fullest extent possible, the Act of 2000, read with the Nitimala in general and Chapter 7 of the Nitimala in particular, has kept the threshold of limitation on such process very low indeed. Limitations in the form of quantum of equity or shareholders the nature and status of the enterprise to be privatised and the supposed lack of the respondent No. 1 Commission's authority to act in a given case as have formed the crux of the petitioner's case before us are not reflected in the provisions of either the Act or the Nitimala. The permissive and liberal regime for privatisation as envisaged by the Act and the Nitimala are borne out by the following three provisions in the Nitimala which negate the existence of limitations of the nature and extent contended by the petitioner to be in existence.
